description: A numeric backreference to an undefined group is refused by the baseline descriptor and by validation here.
descriptor: { descriptor_version: "1.0", root: { type: "object", children: { a: { type: "string", pattern: "(a)\\2" } } } }

divergence.note: docs/grammars.md §1.2 and §1.3 fix which layer reports each regex construct, and §1.2 states that the two implementations can name the same problem at different layers while the outcome (refused, named, never guessed at) does not differ. This is a documented, intentional divergence from the executed baseline under that rule (SPEC.md amendment 26), not a baseline defect.  The baseline engine refuses an undefined group reference at compile time, so its descriptor check refuses the file; this engine compiles it, so the dialect scan names the backreference at validation as the docs §1.2 numeric-backreference row prescribes. Both refuse; the layer differs.
